title: Strict potentialism in modal mirrors
summary: Potentialism is the view that objects are successively generated in an incompletable process. A strict version of the view adds that truths are successively determined. Strict potentialism can be analyzed using two modalities: one for the generation of objects, another for truths becoming determined. The result is a classical bimodal logic. We obtain simpler and more user-friendly theories by invoking so-called mirroring theorems to ``switch off'' one or both modalities, in return for a less classical logic.
